children: China's real GDP growth will likely ease to 4.4% on year in 2027 from 4.6% amid household deleveraging and fiscal restraint, Morgan Stanley analysts say in a note. Nominal growth should slow to 4.8% as energy pressures and chip-related inflation fade and core inflation softens, they add. Despite robust exports, the shadow of past credit expansions sustain the K-shaped economy, they say. AI and Asia's capex supercycle should sustain exports, giving Beijing room to advance economic transition and limiting prospects for a consumption pivot, they add. China's tech investment is likely to remain resilient next year. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
